Lecture 7. Optimization for Neural Networks

7.1 Gradient Descent
Let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be the parameter vector, $\alpha > 0$ the learning rate, and $L(\theta)$ the training loss.
The update rule is
$$\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t - \alpha \nabla_\theta L(\theta_t)$$
In SGD the gradient is estimated on a mini-batch $B$ with $|B| = m$ examples:
$$\nabla_\theta L \approx \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i \in B} \nabla_\theta \ell(x_i, y_i; \theta)$$

7.2 Momentum
Momentum keeps an exponentially decayed average of past gradients with coefficient $\beta \in [0, 1)$:
$$v_{t+1} = \beta v_t + (1 - \beta) \nabla_\theta L(\theta_t), \qquad \theta_{t+1} = \theta_t - \alpha v_{t+1}$$
Typical values are $\beta = 0.9$ and $\alpha = 10^{-3}$.

7.3 Softmax
For a logit vector $z \in \mathbb{R}^K$ the softmax is
$$\sigma(z)_i = \frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_{j=1}^{K} e^{z_j}}$$
so that $\sum_{i=1}^{K} \sigma(z)_i = 1$ and $\sigma(z)_i > 0$ for every $i$.

7.4 Cross-Entropy
For a one-hot target $y$ and prediction $\hat{y} = \sigma(z)$ the cross-entropy loss is
$$L = -\sum_{i=1}^{K} y_i \log \hat{y}_i$$
Its gradient with respect to the logits collapses to $\partial L / \partial z = \hat{y} - y$, which is why softmax and cross-entropy are fused into a single op.

7.5 Learning Rate Schedule
Step decay multiplies $\alpha$ by $\gamma = 0.1$ every $s$ epochs: $\alpha_t = \alpha_0 \gamma^{\lfloor t / s \rfloor}$.
Cosine annealing instead follows $\alpha_t = \alpha_{\min} + \frac{1}{2}(\alpha_0 - \alpha_{\min})(1 + \cos(\pi t / T))$.
